70	### Terminal *content* accessibility (macapp) — CMT-3
71	
72	**What:** VoiceOver support for the terminal's *rendered text* on `GhosttySurfaceView` — accessible
73	value (screen text), selected text, and change notifications — so the terminal content is navigable
74	with assistive tech.
75	
76	**Done so far:** the **UI-tree** a11y has landed (commit `f3859f9`) — `PaneTreeView` exposes each
77	leaf as `terminal.pane` with a label ("Terminal <title>, pane N of M"), a focused/selected trait, and
78	an adjustable split divider (`pane.grip`). That claim is unqualified: the one caveat raised against it
79	(the tab strips' glyph buttons reporting `isHittable == false`) was investigated and closed as an
80	XCUITest artefact — see **Recently done**. What's still missing is the *content* layer: the
81	libghostty surface is Metal-rendered, so its text is pixels — invisible to the accessibility system.
82	Today the surface view sets `role=.textArea` + a label only; it exposes **no value and no selection**,
83	so VoiceOver reads nothing inside the terminal. Accepted regression for the beta (CMT-3). This is also
84	the **enabler for content-level UI tests**: once terminal text is in the a11y tree, XCUITest can
85	assert on rendered output (backspace deleted, TUI drew, scrollback) on top of the now-landed fixture
86	seam — see `macapp/QA-libghostty.md` (Bucket 2).
87	
88	**When:** **sequence with the xcframework upgrade** (CMT-2), not now. Feasible on 1.2.3 today (read
89	APIs exist), but ghostty upstream has merged a11y plumbing we'd want to ride — e.g.
90	**ghostty #12902** ("core: send selection_changed notification"), which on macOS posts
91	`.ghosttySelectionDidChange` → debounced → `NSAccessibility.selectedTextChanged`. On 1.2.3 we'd have
92	to post that notification ourselves on our own selection events; post-upgrade it comes from the
93	engine. A before-GA item.
94	
95	**How to start (minimal-viable, keep light per D1 — crib Muxy's `accessibilitySelectedText()`):**
96	- `accessibilityValue()` → visible screen text via `ghostty_surface_read_text(surface, <viewport
97	  ghostty_selection_s>, …)` (reuse the `extractString(from:)` helper).
98	- `accessibilitySelectedText()` → `ghostty_surface_read_selection` (the same read that powers
99	  copy-on-select).
100	- Post `NSAccessibility.post(element:notification:)` `.selectedTextChanged` on selection change
101	  (we already detect mouseUp / copy-on-select) and a throttled `.valueChanged` on output so
102	  VoiceOver follows along; keep the role/label and report focus.
103	- Skip the full `NSAccessibility` text protocol (line/char-range/bounds geometry) — overkill for a
104	  terminal, and Muxy keeps it minimal too.
105	
106	**Caveat:** terminal a11y is inherently partial (dynamic output, scrollback, full-screen TUIs);
107	target "announce output + selection, navigable text", not a perfect document model.
108	
109	**Depends on:** the read APIs already present in 1.2.3 (`ghostty_surface_read_selection`,

115	## P2 — perf, correctness, and the next VCS phase
116	
117	### VCS write actions — Phase 2 (macapp) — roadmap pointer
118	
119	**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. **Fetch, push
120	and pull-with-rebase have SHIPPED** (the VCS toolbar), and so have **commit + message-only amend/describe**
121	(the Changes inspector's commit dialog). What remains: selection-aware amend (needs a temp index),
122	bookmark (jj) / branch (git) management, and the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog,
123	interdiff).
124	
125	**Where the write seam actually is — this changed.** The original plan put write methods on
126	`VCSProviding` with a `CLIVCSProvider` fallback. That is **not** what shipped, and new work should not
127	follow it. Writes live behind a **separate** `VCSWriting` protocol (`Core/VCSWriting.swift`) with its
128	own factory `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by `CLIVCSWriter`. Two reasons, both load-bearing:
129	
130	- `VCSProviding`'s doc calls it "the single seam the app **reads** VCS data through", and four
131	  resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no gate. A `fetch` on that protocol means
132	  nothing structurally stops a read path firing a network mutation — the opposite of what
133	  `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee.
134	- A CLI-backed method needs an injected `StatusCommandRunning`, and `GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are
135	  stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one. A new conformer has
136	  somewhere.
137	
138	So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
139	environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.
140	
141	**Which backend each op uses — decided, don't re-litigate.** `VCSWriting` says *where* writes live,
142	not *how* they run. The split:
143	
144	| Ops | Backend | Why |
145	|---|---|---|
146	| commit/amend — **CLI, decided against this table's original answer** | **CLI** (`CLIVCSWriter.commit`, shipped) | This row used to say "native", and that was wrong on three counts it never weighed. **libgit2 runs no hooks** ([#964](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/issues/964)) — a `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` that the user's terminal honours would be silently skipped, which is worse than not offering commit at all. **libgit2 cannot sign**, so `commit.gpgsign = true` would produce unsigned commits. And native jj commit is blocked on `immutable_heads()` being a jj-*cli* revset alias that jj-lib cannot resolve — so it would happily rewrite commits the user's own `jj` refuses to touch. (The empty-committer and dropped-signature halves of that third blocker are now fixed by `jj_config.rs`; the revset one is not.) |
147	| branch + bookmark management, jj undo/op-log/split/absorb/evolog | **native** (libgit2/SwiftGitX, jj-lib) — provisional | Local, typed APIs, no output to parse, no tool-version floor, no locale exposure. Still the default answer, but **not "don't re-litigate"**: commit was re-litigated on measurement and moved. Check each op for hooks, signing, and revset aliases before assuming native. |
148	| fetch, push, pull | **CLI** — permanently, not a stopgap | Three independent blockers, all verified from checked-out sources: SwiftGitX passes NULL options (`git_remote_fetch(remotePointer, nil, nil, nil)`, and `pull` is a `// TODO`), so it has no credential callback at all; **libgit2 implements no `credential.helper` protocol** — nothing in its `src` reads that config key, so native auth means reimplementing helper invocation ourselves; and jj-lib shells to `git` for remote ops anyway (that's where its `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION` comes from), so a "native jj push" is a git subprocess wearing a Rust coat. |
149	
150	**Non-goal: Workroom does not store credentials.** No OAuth client, no keychain writes, no auth
151	prompt, no account concept. The user's own helpers (`osxkeychain`, GCM, `!gh auth git-credential`,
152	anything corporate) are the correct answer, and shelling out gets every host — including ones we've
153	never heard of — for free, with the same credentials their terminal uses. GitHub Desktop is the
154	instructive counterexample: it also shells out (via `dugite`, which bundles its own git), but blanks
155	your helpers and registers itself as `credential.helper=desktop` because being *the GitHub client* is
156	its product. The cost of that choice is `app/src/lib/generic-git-auth.ts` — a second credential store,
157	with its own prompt UI, keychain keys and invalidation, for every non-GitHub host. We are not that
158	product, and the app's one GitHub dependency (PR status) already rides `gh`'s own token.
159	
160	**When you do shell out, never parse prose.** `--porcelain`, `-z`, `%(…)`, `-T`, exit codes. Measured:
161	`Updates were rejected` becomes `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées` under `fr_FR.UTF-8`, so a prose
162	match loses the whole failure taxonomy for a non-English user. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C`
163	as a backstop; it is not the plan.
164	
165	*Filed, not planned:* bundling our own `git` the way `dugite` does would delete all of
166	`Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` — floor, probe, notification, per-VCS scoping. Real cost (universal
167	binary, notarization, ~40MB, and the Go CLI would want the same binary), so revisit only if the
168	version floor actually bites a user.
169	
170	**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up. The authoritative scope + sequencing live
171	in the issue #59 plan; this entry is the pointer that makes it discoverable.
172	
173	**How to start:** Read `Core/VCSWriting.swift` — its doc comment carries the routing diagram, the
174	per-backend command table and the placement rules (fetch always runs at the project root, for both
175	backends; jj push too, because bookmarks are repo-global). The read layer blocks nothing. What's left
176	of the error taxonomy is one-sided (git still flattens to `.io`), and the stale-working-copy **repair**
177	is itself a write, so it belongs to this phase.
178	
179	**Depends on:** the VCS read foundation (shipped, Phase 1) and the write seam (shipped with the
180	toolbar). Spans `Core/VCSWriting.swift`, possibly `vcs/` (Rust) + `WrVcs` UniFFI for native jj ops, and
181	new write-flow UI.
182	
183	**Priority:** P2 (the product direction; large — see the plan for the real breakdown).

185	### `withTimeout` doesn't observe the CALLER's own cancellation (macapp) — VCS-foundation eng-review, /review follow-up
186	
187	**Status:** the original version of this entry (a `withThrowingTaskGroup` awaiting a detached
188	operation child past its own deadline) is **fixed** — `Core/Timeout.swift` now races via a single
189	`withCheckedThrowingContinuation` + a `TimeoutGate`, exactly the fix this entry used to recommend.
190	Re-audited during the jj-snapshot-serialization `/review` (2026-07-24, cross-model: Codex found it)
191	and found a **different, still-live** gap in that same seam.
192	
193	**What:** `withTimeout`'s `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` only resolves on ITS OWN internal race
194	(the operation finishing vs. its own `seconds` deadline firing) — it never wires up
195	`withTaskCancellationHandler`, so it does not observe the CALLING task being cancelled from outside.
196	Concretely: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`'s `statusSweepTask?.cancel()` (a new sweep replacing an
197	old one) propagates into `runLocalSweep`'s `withTaskGroup` children structurally, but a cancelled
198	child's in-flight `withTimeout(seconds:) { … }` call (inside `resolveJJ`/`resolveGit`) keeps running
199	to completion (or its own `seconds` timeout) regardless — it doesn't stop early just because the
200	enclosing task gave up.
201	
202	**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
203	fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
204	caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). Not corruption-causing
205	today: every call site already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result
206	(`runLocalSweep`'s `if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.), so state stays correct — this is a
207	responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one.
208	
209	**How to start:** Wrap `withTimeout`'s continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` so cancelling
210	the calling task settles the `TimeoutGate` early (same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run` already uses to
211	propagate cancellation into its own chained `Task`). Verify the existing "operation keeps running,
212	result dropped" contract still holds — this only makes the WAIT responsive to cancellation, not the
213	underlying synchronous native call (still uncancellable, unchanged).
214	
215	**Depends on:** —. Touches `Core/Timeout.swift`. Broad blast radius (every `withTimeout` caller:
216	`WorkroomStatusResolver`, `BranchResolver`, `JJSnapshotGate`'s own internal use) — needs its own
217	careful review/testing, not a drive-by fix.
218	
219	**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).
220	
221	### VCS toolbar: ten confirmed findings the `/review` pass didn't fix (macapp)
222	
223	**What:** Everything the toolbar review verified but left standing. Each was reproduced or read off the
224	code; none is speculative. Ordered by what a user hits first.
225	
226	1. **A configured remote with NO refs reads as "No remote configured".** `primaryRemote` is derived
227	   purely from `refs/remotes` rows, and a fresh empty remote has none (verified: `for-each-ref
228	   refs/remotes` = 0 lines; jj's `bookmark list --all-remotes` likewise empty). So `canPush` is false and
229	   publishing to a brand-new empty GitHub repo — the case where "Publish branch" matters most — is
230	   impossible from the app. Fix: take the remote LIST from config (`git remote`, and jj's remotes) while
231	   leaving the counts ref-derived.
232	2. **jj Pull guesses `trunk()` as the base for an unbookmarked `@`.** Right for a workroom off trunk,
233	   wrong for one off a feature branch: it reports "N behind" counting trunk's commits and the rebase
234	   then refuses (`immutableHistory`, now typed and retry-free, so it fails honestly rather than looping).
235	   The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base rather than deriving it — `::@ &
236	   remote_bookmarks()` can't, because the base stops being an ancestor the moment it advances.
237	3. **jj bookmark names that need quoting never match.** jj's template pre-quotes non-identifier names
238	   (verified: `"main|evil"` comes back WITH the quotes), so `parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }`
239	   compares `"main|evil"` against jj-lib's raw `main|evil` and always fails — tracking, counts and Pull
240	   go silently nil. Parse names unquoted, and build the rebase destination from `(name, remote)` with
241	   `jjQuote` on each rather than reusing the pre-joined `comparedTo` display string.
242	4. **jj multi-remote: the wrong remote's tracking row wins.** `trackingByName[name] = …` overwrites by
243	   name with no `primaryRemote` filter, so with `origin` + `upstream` both tracking `main` the last row
244	   read decides the counts while every UI string interpolates `primaryRemote`. The git path builds
245	   `"\(primary)/\(branch)"` explicitly; jj is the asymmetry. Same root cause makes `@..trunk()` capable
246	   of counting against a different remote than the one it names and fetches.
247	5. **`resolvedBranchNames` is stale-wins and never pruned.** It's now source #1 for every
248	   branch-showing surface but is written only for the focused target, never removed on workroom/project
249	   delete, and its refresh is gated on the inspector being visible AND on Changes. So `git switch` in a
250	   workroom's terminal leaves the sidebar and status bar showing the old name indefinitely.
251	6. **A failure is discarded if the selection moved.** `finish` guards the `lastFailure` write on target
252	   identity (correct for rendering), and there is no toast for VCS action failures — so a push that
253	   fails after you switch workrooms is recorded nowhere. You saw a spinner and never learn it didn't
254	   happen.
255	7. **A failed remote READ renders "No repository".** Nothing renders `model.state`; the toolbar reads
256	   `snapshot` (nil'd on failure) and `lastFailure` (set only by actions). So a read blocked by
257	   `packed-refs.lock`, or any `.other`, shows tier `[2]` with no diagnosis and no retry. Compounding it,
258	   `RemoteStateModel.activate` — documented as "the panel's `.task`" and the only non-forced refresh
259	   caller — is called by no view at all.
260	8. **A workroom deleted mid-action reports "git isn't on Workroom's PATH".** `StatusCommandRunner`
261	   returns `commandNotFound` for a launch failure ("cwd vanished" per its own comment) and `classify`
262	   maps that exit code to `.toolMissing`, which offers no recovery — while the version toast
263	   simultaneously says git is fine. Launch failure needs its own sentinel.
264	9. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s 30s self-heal is far below the write timeouts it guards.** The gate accepts
265	   re-admitting the original race past `maxChainWait`, justified as "the rare genuine-wedge case, not
266	   routine contention" — but fetch is budgeted at 120s and pull at 300s, so exceeding 30s is routine.
267	   Two windows, each with its own `AppStore` and its own `inFlight`, can queue two writes on one project
268	   root; the second gives up and runs concurrently with a live `pull --rebase` on the shared `.git`.
269	10. **Colocated jj root: "Abort rebase" reports success, changes nothing, loops.** `classify` can hand a
270	    colocated root `.rebaseInProgress` from a `rebase-merge` left by a `git rebase` in its terminal, and
271	    the jj branch of `abortRebase` returns `.ok(summary: "Nothing to abort")` — so `finish` clears the
272	    failure, the user pulls, and the identical failure returns.
273	
274	Plus one doc correction: `gitLastFetch`'s comment claims `FETCH_HEAD`'s mtime covers "one the user ran in
275	a terminal". It doesn't, for the terminals this app opens — a fetch inside a worktree writes
276	`worktrees/<n>/FETCH_HEAD` while the common one stays put (measured), so counts update from the shared
277	`refs/remotes` while the timestamp doesn't. Either read both and take the max, or stop claiming it.
278	
279	**Why:** These are the residue of a five-pass review (critical + 4 specialists + Claude adversarial +
280	Codex) whose P0s — argv option injection and jj push publishing the wrong workspace's commit — are
281	already fixed. What's left is real but none of it is a security hole or silent data loss.
282	
283	**Priority:** P2. (1), (5) and (7) are the ones a user notices.

285	### Gate git VCS *reads*, not just writes (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up
286	
287	**What:** Route git status reads through the same per-project `JJSnapshotGate` the writes now use.
288	
289	**Why:** The toolbar's write path gates git as well as jj, because a project's workrooms are
290	`git worktree add` worktrees sharing ONE `.git` — a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a workroom
291	wedged in a rebase. But that only half-closes the contention: `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit`
292	never touches the gate (only `resolveJJ` does), so a fetch writing `packed-refs` while the ungated
293	status sweep runs `git status` across N sibling worktrees reproduces exactly the
294	`packed-refs.lock could not be obtained` failure the gate's own doc cites.
295	
296	**Pros:** removes the last window where `.locked` is an *expected* outcome rather than an anomaly, so
297	the UI's Retry affordance becomes a genuine edge case.
298	
299	**Cons:** serialising reads could measurably slow the status sweep, which fans out per workroom by
300	design. This wants measurement first — it may be that read/write contention is rare enough in practice
301	that the cost isn't worth it.
302	
303	**Context / how to start:** `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit` (the ungated read) vs `resolveJJ` (the
304	gated one); `CLIVCSWriter.gated` for how the writes do it. Note the gate is key-based and
305	backend-agnostic, so if this lands, renaming `JJSnapshotGate` → `RepoWriteGate` (3 call sites + its
306	test suite) stops being speculative churn and starts being accurate.
307	
308	**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).
309	
310	**Priority:** P3 (a real but narrow race; needs measurement before it's worth the sweep's latency).
311	
312	### jj sibling-workspace staleness after a rebase (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up
313	
314	**What:** Detect and surface when a jj operation in one workroom leaves a *sibling* workspace stale.
315	
316	**Why:** All workrooms of a jj project share one repo and op-store. `jj rebase -b @` — what
317	pull-with-rebase runs — rewrites commits, and any other workspace whose `@` descends from a rewritten
318	commit is marked stale and needs `jj workspace update-stale` before its next command. Today that
319	surfaces as an unexplained error in a **different** workroom from the one the user acted in, which is
320	the worst attribution problem available: nothing on screen connects cause to effect.
321	
322	**Pros:** turns a mystery error into an explained one, and the repair is a single command Workroom

559	  old code.

561	  `can_sign()` was false and a rewrite of an already-signed `@` discarded its signature under the
562	  default `behavior = "keep"`. Now works for free, since the signer is built from these settings.

572	Original description follows.

635	being visible with the Changes section active, skipped entirely under the UI-test fixture, and silent

638	**What's LEFT:** the two things this entry originally said were the reason not to "just add a fetch" —
639	a real cadence policy (a periodic timer, not only focus) and a **Settings toggle** to turn it off. The
640	5-minute interval is currently a hardcoded constant with no UI. Also worth revisiting: whether an
641	unattended machine should auto-fetch at all, which is a preference question, not a technical one.
642	
643	**Why the staleness reasoning below still stands:** it is the clearest writeup of the problem in the
644	repo, and the toolbar's ahead/behind counts inherit it exactly — they are computed from local
645	remote-tracking refs, so they are only as fresh as the last fetch. That is why the toolbar shows "last
646	fetched N ago" beside the counts rather than presenting them as fact.
647	
648	---
649	
650	**What (original):** A periodic / on-focus `git fetch` (and `jj git fetch`) so remote-tracking refs —
651	and therefore the History pane's unpushed badge — reflect the server rather than the last manual fetch.
652	
653	**Why:** Every push-state answer in the app is local knowledge: `GitGraph` walks
654	`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*` and the jj core evaluates `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)`.
655	Neither touches the network. So a commit pushed from another machine keeps its badge until you fetch,
656	and a commit that was force-pushed away still reads as pushed. The badge tooltip is honest about this
657	("based on your local remote-tracking refs"), but admitting it isn't fixing it.
658	
659	**Pros:** The badge (and anything later built on the same reads — ahead/behind counts, a push action)
660	becomes truthful without the user doing anything.
661	
662	**Cons:** This turns a pure local read into a network feature: auth prompts for private remotes, rate
663	limits, timeouts, and partial failures on a path that today cannot fail. It needs a cadence policy and
664	almost certainly a Settings toggle — "just add a fetch" is the wrong shape.
665	
666	**Context / how to start:** The read path itself needs no change — a fetch only has to write refs; the
667	per-project watcher (`AppStore.handleRootBranchChange`, which watches each project's `.git`/`.jj`) then
668	repaints History automatically, exactly as it does after a local push. So the work is entirely about
669	*when* to fetch and how to fail quietly: pick the trigger (app focus + an interval), keep it off the
670	synchronous log-read path, decide the credential story (the status sweep already shells `gh`, so there

672	the badge: see the "Staleness" trap in the unpushed-badge plan.

# TODOS recommendation shortlist

## Context

Joel asked for a couple of recommended items from `TODOS.md`. Ranked by user-visible
impact per unit of effort, verified against the current code rather than taken from the
entry text.

**Stale entry found:** P2 "VCS toolbar: ten confirmed findings" item **(1)** — "a configured
remote with NO refs reads as No remote configured" — is **already fixed**.
`CLIVCSWriter.mergeRemotes` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift:1470-1483`) unions the
configured remote list (`git remote` / `jj git remote list`) with the ref-derived names, and both
`gitRemoteState` and `jjRemoteState` call it. That bullet should be struck from TODOS.

## Recommendation 1 — VCS toolbar honesty cluster (P2; findings 5, 6, 7)

One seam, three user-noticeable defects:

- **Stale branch name.** `AppStore.resolvedBranchNames` (`Core/AppStore.swift:632`) is written only
  by `RemoteStateModel` for the *focused* target, and `focusRemoteStateIfShown`
  (`Core/AppStore.swift:392`) gates that on `inspectorIsVisible && activeInspectorSection == .changes`.
  Nothing prunes it on workroom/project delete. `git switch` in a workroom terminal leaves the
  sidebar + status bar (`branchName(for:)`, `Core/AppStore.swift:1544`) showing the old name.
- **Silent action failure.** `RemoteStateModel.finish` guards the `lastFailure` write on target
  identity, and there is no toast for VCS action failures — a push that fails after you switch
  workrooms is recorded nowhere.
- **Failed read misdiagnosed.** Nothing renders `model.state`; the toolbar reads `snapshot`
  (nil'd on failure) and `lastFailure` (set only by actions), so a read blocked by
  `packed-refs.lock` shows "No repository" with no diagnosis and no retry. Compounding it,
  `RemoteStateModel.activate` (`Core/RemoteStateModel.swift:122`) — documented as "the panel's
  `.task`" — is **called by no view** (verified: only `HistoryModel`/`FilesModel` `activate` have
  callers, in `HistoryPanel.swift:87` / `FilesPanel.swift:47`).

Files: `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift`, `Core/AppStore.swift`, `Views/VCSToolbar.swift`,
`Views/ChangesPanel.swift`. No backend/Rust work. Existing pieces to reuse: the toast stack
(`ToastStack`), `setResolvedBranchName(nil, for:)` for pruning, `VCSStatusFailure` taxonomy for
the diagnosis text.

## Recommendation 2 — `DiffDescriptor.change` goes stale (P3; small, net deletion)

`change` is captured at diff-tab open and never refreshed, yet `DiffViewer` paints it as the header
letter and `TerminalTabStrip` disables "Open file in…" when it is `.deleted`. Live answer already
exists in `WorkroomStatus.changedFiles` (one lookup serves git and jj). Landing it lets
`AppStore.refreshingChangeKind` be deleted. Watch the WORKROOM-2B row-invalidation hot path: the
strip and viewer must not subscribe to a high-frequency publisher to get it.

## Runner-up (not recommended as a "couple of items")

**CMT-2 — own the GhosttyKit xcframework.** The real P1 before GA, and the packager lag is real
(libghostty-spm on 1.2.3 vs ghostty 1.3.1), but it is an infra project, not an afternoon.

## Next step

Awaiting Joel's pick before writing the executable plan for the chosen item.

219	  /// the writer and the gate are shared. Only the LABEL is per-target.
220	  var activeAction: VCSRemoteAction? { inFlightTarget == target ? inFlight : nil }
221	
222	  var canFetch: Bool { snapshot?.primaryRemote != nil && inFlight == nil }
223	  var canPush: Bool { snapshot?.primaryRemote != nil && inFlight == nil }
224	  /// Pull needs something to pull FROM: a counterpart that exists on the remote.
225	  var canPull: Bool {
226	    guard snapshot?.primaryRemote != nil, inFlight == nil else { return false }
227	    guard let tracking = snapshot?.tracking else { return false }
228	    return !tracking.gone
229	  }
230	
231	  func canPerform(_ action: VCSRemoteAction) -> Bool {
232	    switch action {
233	    case .fetch: return canFetch
234	    case .push: return canPush
235	    case .pull: return canPull
236	    case .abortRebase: return inFlight == nil
237	    }
238	  }
239	
240	  // MARK: Actions
241	
242	  /// Perform an action. Dropped if one is already in flight — the model is deliberately single-action
243	  /// so a double-click can't fire twice and Push can't race Pull.
244	  ///
245	  /// `anonymousRevision` matters only for a jj workroom whose `@` carries no bookmark: pushing a bare
246	  /// `@` fails when the working copy is empty and undescribed, which is exactly the state a fresh
247	  /// workroom sits in. Callers pass `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)`.
248	  ///
249	  /// `userInitiated` decides whether a failure gets a dialog. Only `autoFetchIfDue` passes `false`.
250	  func perform(
251	    _ action: VCSRemoteAction, setUpstream: Bool = false, anonymousRevision: String = "@",
252	    userInitiated: Bool = true
253	  ) {
254	    guard inFlight == nil, let target, let snapshot else { return }
255	    // Aborting a rebase is purely local — requiring a remote would leave a workroom wedged in a rebase
256	    // with no way out from the UI, which is the one state where recovery matters most.
257	    let remote = snapshot.primaryRemote ?? ""
258	    if remote.isEmpty, action != .abortRebase {
259	      lastFailure = .noRemote
260	      lastAction = action
261	      if userInitiated { raiseFailureReport(.noRemote, action: action) }
262	      return
263	    }
264	    inFlight = action
265	    inFlightTarget = target
266	    lastAction = action
267	    lastFailure = nil
268	    failureReport = nil
269	    lastPullConflicted = false
270	    let makeWriter = self.makeWriter
271	    let current = snapshot.current
272	    let tracking = snapshot.tracking
273	    actionTask = Task { [weak self] in
274	      let root = URL(fileURLWithPath: target.path, isDirectory: true)
275	      let result: VCSRemoteActionResult
276	      do {
277	        let writer = try makeWriter(root)
278	        switch action {
279	        case .fetch:
280	          result = await writer.fetch(
281	            path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot, remote: remote)
282	        case .push:
283	          result = await writer.push(
284	            path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot, current: current, remote: remote,
285	            setUpstream: setUpstream, anonymousRevision: anonymousRevision)
286	        case .pull:
287	          result = await writer.pullRebase(
288	            path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot, current: current, remote: remote,
289	            tracking: tracking)
290	        case .abortRebase:
291	          result = await writer.abortRebase(path: target.path, projectRoot: target.projectRoot)
292	        }
293	      } catch {
294	        result = .failed(.other("\(error)"))
295	      }
296	      self?.finish(action, result: result, for: target, userInitiated: userInitiated)
297	    }
298	  }
299	
300	  private func finish(
301	    _ action: VCSRemoteAction, result: VCSRemoteActionResult, for target: Target,
302	    userInitiated: Bool
303	  ) {
304	    // Always cleared: the action really is over, and this is the model-wide single-action lock. What is
305	    // NOT unconditional is the RESULT, below.
306	    inFlight = nil
307	    inFlightTarget = nil
308	    // The work happened in `target`'s repo whatever is selected now, so the fetch stamp and the
309	    // downstream refresh belong to it and fire regardless.
310	    if case .ok = result {
311	      if action == .fetch || action == .pull { recordOwnFetch(projectRoot: target.projectRoot) }
312	      onDidMutate?(action, target.sid)
313	    }
314	    // Everything past here writes PUBLISHED state that the toolbar renders for whatever is selected NOW,
315	    // so it needs the same guard `apply` has. Without it, starting a push in one workroom and switching
316	    // to another put the first one's failure — and its action label — on the second one's toolbar,
317	    // reporting a failure for a workroom where nothing was attempted.
318	    guard self.target == target else { return }
319	    switch result {
320	    case .ok:
321	      lastFailure = nil
322	      // Re-read immediately AND let the store refresh everything downstream. The metadata watcher
323	      // would get there on its own, but its coalesce window is ~1s and the toolbar should feel instant.
324	      refresh(force: true)
325	    case .failed(let failure):
326	      // Deliberately leaves `snapshot` intact: a failed action tells you nothing new about the repo.
327	      lastFailure = failure
328	      if userInitiated { raiseFailureReport(failure, action: action) }
329	    }
330	  }
331	
332	  /// Put a failure in front of the user. The toolbar's one truncating line can't carry the message, so
333	  /// anything the user asked for and that failed gets the dialog.
334	  private func raiseFailureReport(_ failure: VCSRemoteFailure, action: VCSRemoteAction?) {
335	    failureSequence += 1
336	    failureReport = VCSFailureReport(
337	      failure: failure, action: action, sequence: failureSequence)
338	  }
339	
340	  /// Re-open the dialog for the failure the toolbar is currently reporting — the segment's "Show Error
341	  /// Details…" item. No-op when there is nothing to show.
342	  func presentFailureDetails() {
343	    guard let lastFailure else { return }
344	    raiseFailureReport(lastFailure, action: lastAction)
345	  }
346	
347	  /// Close the dialog. `lastFailure` deliberately survives: the bar goes on reporting the failure until
348	  /// the next action or refresh, so dismissing the dialog doesn't erase the fact that something failed.
349	  func dismissFailureReport() {
350	    failureReport = nil
351	  }
352	
353	  /// Stamp Workroom's own fetch time for this project. See `merging` for why this exists.
354	  private func recordOwnFetch(projectRoot: String) {
355	    var stamps = Defaults[.vcsLastFetch]
356	    stamps[projectRoot] = now()
357	    Defaults[.vcsLastFetch] = stamps
358	  }
359	
360	  /// Called by the store after the post-mutation status refresh lands: a pull that reported success may
361	  /// still have produced conflicts (jj writes them into commits and exits 0).
362	  /// `sid` is the workroom the pull ran in — checked, not trusted, for the same reason `finish` checks it:
363	  /// the sweep this waits on is async, so the selection can move before it lands.
364	  func noteConflictState(_ conflicted: Bool, for sid: SidebarID) {
365	    guard target?.sid == sid, lastAction == .pull, lastFailure == nil else { return }
366	    lastPullConflicted = conflicted
367	  }
368	
369	  // MARK: Auto-fetch
370	
371	  /// Fetch when the inspector gains focus, at most once per `autoFetchInterval` per project.
372	  ///
373	  /// Automatic, so it must be quiet: a failure sets `lastFailure` for the toolbar but raises no dialog
374	  /// (`userInitiated: false`) and never blocks the read path. Callers gate on the inspector being visible
375	  /// with the Changes section active, so a hidden toolbar never triggers a network call.
376	  func autoFetchIfDue() {
377	    guard let target, inFlight == nil, let snapshot, snapshot.primaryRemote != nil else { return }
378	    if let last = lastAutoFetch[target.projectRoot],
379	      now().timeIntervalSince(last) < autoFetchInterval
380	    {
381	      return
382	    }
383	    lastAutoFetch[target.projectRoot] = now()
384	    perform(.fetch, userInitiated: false)
385	  }

# Two TODOS items: VCS toolbar honesty cluster + live diff change kind

## Context

Joel asked for a couple of recommended `TODOS.md` items; he picked **both** of the two
highest-leverage ones, plus correcting the TODOS entry that is now stale.

Every claim below was re-verified against the code, not taken from the entry text. That check found
one entry already fixed and three still live:

- **STALE — P2 toolbar finding (1)** ("a configured remote with NO refs reads as No remote
  configured") is **fixed**. `CLIVCSWriter.mergeRemotes`
  (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift:1470-1483`) unions the configured remote list with the
  ref-derived names, and both `gitRemoteState` (`:1371`) and `jjRemoteState` (`:1411`) call it.
- **LIVE — finding (5)**, stale/unpruned branch name.
- **LIVE — finding (6)**, but narrower than filed: the failure *dialog* shipped
  (`raiseFailureReport`), so the gap is only the case where the selection moved.
- **LIVE — finding (7)**, failed *read* renders "No repository", and `RemoteStateModel.activate` has
  no caller.

Outcome wanted: the toolbar and sidebar stop asserting things that aren't true, and an open diff tab
stops acting on a change kind captured at open time.

---

## Part 1 — VCS toolbar honesty cluster (P2)

### 1a. Stale branch name (finding 5)

**Diagnosis.** `AppStore.resolvedBranchNames` (`Core/AppStore.swift:632`) is source #1 of
`branchName(for:)` (`:1544`) — the single accessor the sidebar, status bar, Changes header and
toolbar all read. It is written only by `RemoteStateModel` via `onBranchResolved`, only for the
*focused* target, and only when `focusRemoteStateIfShown` (`:392`) sees
`inspectorIsVisible && activeInspectorSection == .changes`. Nothing invalidates it when a lower,
fresher source disagrees, and nothing removes it on delete. So `git switch` in a workroom terminal
leaves every surface showing the old branch indefinitely.

**Fix — two edits, both in `AppStore`:**

1. **Drift-prune in `mergeLocalStatus`** (`Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:517`, the one hook
   where a fresh local sweep lands). After `s.branchForCI = fresh.branchForCI`: if
   `resolvedBranchNames[sid]` is non-nil and disagrees with a non-empty `fresh.branchForCI`, call
   `setResolvedBranchName(nil, for: sid)`. Rationale: the cache's whole justification (its doc at
   `:1538`) is "freshest first" — the moment a 15s-TTL sweep contradicts it, it is no longer the
   freshest and must yield rather than win. No new VCS read; `branchName` stays cache-only, which
   `BranchLabelTests` pins with a provider-counting stub.
2. **Prune on delete.** `deleteWorkroom` already clears `workroomStatuses[sid] = nil`
   (`Core/AppStore.swift:2907`) — add `setResolvedBranchName(nil, for: sid)` beside it, and the same
   in `removeProjectLocally` (`:3198`) for the project's root + each workroom sid.

### 1b. A failure vanishes when the selection moved (finding 6)

**Diagnosis.** `finish` (`Core/RemoteStateModel.swift:300`) clears the lock and fires the downstream
refresh unconditionally, then `guard self.target == target else { return }` at `:318` — correct for
`lastFailure`, which the toolbar renders for whatever is selected *now*, but it also skips
`raiseFailureReport`. So a user-initiated push that fails after switching workrooms produces no
dialog, no toolbar notice, and no record: you saw a spinner and never learn it didn't happen.

**Fix.** Move the report out from behind the identity guard for `userInitiated` actions, and make it
attributable rather than ambiguous:

- Add the acting workroom to `VCSFailureReport` (`Core/VCSWriting.swift:99`) — e.g.
  `workroomLabel: String?`, derived from `target.sid`. `VCSFailureSheet`
  (`Views/VCSFailureSheet.swift`) names it in the title/subtitle when it is not the current
  selection, so the dialog can never be read as describing the workroom now on screen.
- In `finish`, on `.failed` with `userInitiated`, raise the report **before** the identity guard;
  keep `lastFailure`/`lastAction` behind it exactly as now.
- Do **not** route this through `enqueueToast`. `WorkroomNotification`
  (`Core/NotificationCenterStore.swift:16`) is OSC-shaped — `targetID` + `tabID` + `kind == .osc` —
  so a VCS failure does not fit it without inventing a second kind. The dialog is already the
  app's answer for "a thing you asked for failed"; the bug is that it is suppressed, not that it is
  the wrong surface.

### 1c. A failed read renders "No repository" (finding 7)

**Diagnosis.** `apply`'s `.failed` case sets `state = .failed(VCSSyncPresenter.describe(failure))`
and nils `snapshot` (`Core/RemoteStateModel.swift:193-197`), but `VCSToolbar` passes only
`state: model.snapshot` and `failure: model.lastFailure` (`Views/VCSToolbar.swift:89-94`) —
`model.state` is rendered nowhere. So a read blocked by `packed-refs.lock` shows the placeholder
tier with no diagnosis and no retry, while `lastFailure` (actions only) stays nil.

**Fix.**

- Surface read failures on the failure tier: pass the read failure into the presenter alongside
  `lastFailure` (a read failure when `lastFailure == nil`), so the bar shows the described cause
  with the existing "Show Error Details…" affordance (`Views/VCSToolbar.swift:134`) and a retry that
  calls `model.refresh(force: true)`. Keep `.keepPrior` behaviour untouched — a blip must still not
  blank a good toolbar.
- Keep the failure typed rather than stringly: store the `VCSRemoteFailure` for the read (not just
  the `describe`d `String` inside `State.failed`) so the tier can pick the right recovery
  (`.locked` → retry) instead of pattern-matching prose.
- **Wire `activate`** (`Core/RemoteStateModel.swift:122`): give `ChangesPanel`'s `VCSToolbar`
  (`Views/ChangesPanel.swift:31`) a `.task(id:)` calling `model.activate(store.remoteTarget())`,
  matching `HistoryPanel.swift:87` and `FilesPanel.swift:47`. That is what its own doc promises, and
  it is what makes the after-a-transient-failure retry happen without a manual poke.

### Files touched (Part 1)

`Core/RemoteStateModel.swift`, `Core/AppStore.swift`, `Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`,
`Core/VCSWriting.swift` (report struct only), `Views/VCSToolbar.swift`,
`Views/VCSFailureSheet.swift`, `Views/ChangesPanel.swift`.

---

## Part 2 — `DiffDescriptor.change` goes stale on any open tab (P3)

**Diagnosis.** `change` (`Core/DiffDescriptor.swift:28`) is captured at tab-open and never
refreshed, yet it is both rendered and acted on: `Views/DiffViewer.swift:157-159` paints it as the
header letter/colour, and `Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:293,872,878` disables "Open file in…" when
it is `.deleted`. Delete a file with its diff tab open and the header still says `M` while the menu
item stays enabled; the inverse wrongly disables it. Replay is already correct
(`AppStore.refreshingChangeKind`, `Core/AppStore.swift:3828`), so Back is currently *more* accurate
than leaving the tab open — backwards.

**Fix — refresh at the source, don't delete the field.** Add a store-side refresher that rewrites
open working-copy diff tabs' descriptors in place, called from `mergeLocalStatus`
(`Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:517`) — the one place `changedFiles` lands:

- For each open tab whose content is `.diff` with source `.gitWorktree` / `.jjWorkingCopy`, look the
  path up in `status.changedFiles` and write the live `change` back, **guarded** so an unchanged kind
  mutates nothing (no per-sweep churn, no needless invalidation — the WORKROOM-2B row-invalidation
  constraint).
- Reuse the predicate already written for replay: `refreshingChangeKind`'s source switch and
  `changedFiles` lookup are exactly the rule wanted here — lift that body into the shared helper
  rather than writing a second copy.
- Then call the same helper at the end of `applyLocation`'s content step and **delete
  `refreshingChangeKind`** plus its three `AppStoreContentNavigationTests` cases (`:476-491`),
  replacing them with tests against the helper. Replay stays correct because it now refreshes
  through the same path.

**Why not remove the field** (as the TODOS entry proposes): `.commit`-source diffs still need a
change kind and live status has no answer for them (the changeset does), and `DiffViewer` takes a
plain `let descriptor` with no store — removing the field would push new store coupling into the
viewer and a new parameter through every call site, including `ChangesetDetailView`. Central refresh
fixes both symptoms with a much smaller blast radius, and keeps `sameFile(as:)` tab identity
(`:37`) untouched since it already excludes `change`.

**Files touched (Part 2)** `Core/AppStore.swift` (helper + `applyLocation`),
`Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift` (call site). No view changes.

---

## Part 3 — correct `TODOS.md`

In the "VCS toolbar: ten confirmed findings" entry:

- **Remove finding (1)** and note in the entry preamble that `mergeRemotes` shipped the config-list
  union for both backends, so the empty-remote case now offers Publish.
- **Narrow finding (6)** to what is actually live: the dialog exists for user-initiated failures;

### `DiffDescriptor.change` goes stale on any open tab (macapp) — nav-history follow-up

**What:** `change` is captured when a diff tab is opened and never refreshed, yet it is both rendered
and acted on: `DiffViewer` paints it as the header letter, and `TerminalTabStrip` disables
"Open file in…" when it is `.deleted`. Remove the field from `DiffDescriptor` and have the viewer and
the strip read the live kind from status instead.

**Why:** leave a diff tab open, delete the file, and the header still says `M` while "Open file in…"
stays enabled for a file that is gone (and the inverse wrongly disables it). The nav-history fix already
solved the replay half — `AppStore.refreshingChangeKind` re-resolves a working-copy diff's kind from
`workroomStatuses` on back/forward — so Back is now *more* correct than leaving the tab open, which is
the wrong way round.

**How to start:** the live answer is `WorkroomStatus.changedFiles`, which already mirrors the jj working
copy's own file list, so one lookup serves git and jj. Doing this lets
`AppStore.refreshingChangeKind` be deleted. Mind the row-invalidation hot path (WORKROOM-2B): the strip
and viewer must not start observing a high-frequency publisher to get it.

**Depends on:** nothing; supersedes `refreshingChangeKind`.

**Priority:** P3 (pre-existing, and the replay path — the one that could newly surprise — is fixed).

### ~~`DiffDescriptor.change` goes stale on any open tab (macapp)~~ — SHIPPED

**What shipped:** the change kind is refreshed at the SOURCE rather than re-derived per surface.
`AppStore.refreshOpenDiffChangeKinds` rewrites every open working-copy diff tab's descriptor from
`WorkroomStatus.changedFiles`, called from `mergeLocalStatus` (where a sweep lands) and after a
back/forward landing; the freshness rule itself is the pure `AppStore.liveChangeKind`, and
`refreshingChangeKind` is gone. So deleting a file with its diff tab open now repaints the header letter
and disables "Open file in…" without the tab being touched.

Two things worth knowing before touching it:

- **The field was deliberately kept.** Removing it (this entry's original proposal) doesn't work:
  `.commit`-source diffs still need a change kind and live status has no answer for them, and
  `DiffViewer` takes a plain `let descriptor` with no store — so removal means new store coupling in the
  viewer plus a new parameter at every call site including `ChangesetDetailView`. Refreshing centrally
  gets both symptoms with none of that, and `sameFile(as:)` tab identity already excludes `change`.
- **The write does NOT go through `setContent`.** `TerminalSessions.refreshDiffChangeKind` mutates the
  descriptor in place and fires no `onTabContentChange`, because that callback RECORDS a back/forward
  entry — a sweep noticing a file went from modified to deleted is not somewhere the user navigated. It
  also returns `false` for an unchanged kind and publishes nothing, so the 15s cadence can't invalidate
  every strip row for free (WORKROOM-2B). Both are pinned by tests.

Condensed from the long status notes this file used to carry at the top; the full write-ups are in git
history. Kept here for the parts that stay useful: what changed, and the traps found doing it.

**2026-08-05 — four caches and surfaces that asserted stale or wrong things.** The three user-noticed
findings from the VCS-toolbar review ((5), (6), (7) — see that entry) plus `DiffDescriptor.change` going
stale on an open tab. What each turned on:

- **A "freshest first" cache needs a way to be retracted.** `resolvedBranchNames` led `branchName(for:)`
  because the toolbar read is normally freshest, but only the FOCUSED target is ever written and only
  while the inspector shows Changes — so nothing could ever say "not any more", and `git switch` in a
  terminal left every surface on the old name indefinitely. Fix is one line at the sweep
  (`pruneResolvedBranchNameIfDrifted`): a lower source that disagrees retracts the higher one. An
  empty/absent swept branch is NOT a disagreement — a detached HEAD and an unbookmarked jj `@` both
  legitimately report none.
- **An identity guard that's right for rendering is wrong for reporting.** `finish` guards its published
  state on target identity because the toolbar renders whatever is selected NOW — correct — but the
  failure DIALOG was behind the same guard, so a push that failed after a workroom switch was reported
  nowhere at all. Raised ahead of the guard now, with the workroom named
  (`VCSFailureReport.workroom`) when it isn't the current selection.
- **A failure described into a `String` is a dead end.** `state.failed(String)` carried the read's
  failure but nothing rendered `state` and nothing could classify a description, so a read blocked by
  `packed-refs.lock` reached the bar as a nil snapshot and rendered "No repository" — a wrong diagnosis
  of a healthy repo. Publishing it typed (`readFailure`) is what let the presenter add tier [13b].
- **Refreshing content must not look like navigating to it.** `TerminalSessions.setContent` fires
  `onTabContentChange`, which RECORDS a back/forward entry — so refreshing an open diff tab's change kind
  through it would have logged a history step every time a file changed under the user. The refresher
  mutates in place, fires nothing, and returns `false` for an unchanged kind so a 15s sweep publishes
  nothing (WORKROOM-2B). Also: `DiffDescriptor.change` was KEPT, not removed as filed — `.commit` diffs
  need a kind that live status can't supply.

content.text:
Both items done and verified. Not committed — say the word.

**Part 1 — toolbar honesty (P2 findings 5, 6, 7)**
- Branch drift: `mergeLocalStatus` retracts `resolvedBranchNames` when the sweep's `branchForCI` disagrees (`pruneResolvedBranchNameIfDrifted`); empty/absent swept branch isn't a disagreement. Pruned on delete in `removeWorkroomLocally` / `removeProjectLocally`, beside the label they already dropped.
- Failure attribution: the dialog now raises **ahead of** `finish`'s identity guard for user-initiated actions, carrying `VCSFailureReport.workroom` so the sheet names where it happened. `lastFailure` stays behind the guard (the bar renders the current selection). No toast — `WorkroomNotification` is OSC-shaped (`targetID`/`tabID`/`kind == .osc`).
- Failed read: `RemoteStateModel.readFailure` publishes it typed; presenter gained tier **[13b]** (below an action failure and in-flight, above the rest) naming the cause, carrying the lock path, offering "Try Again" via `retriesRead` — re-reading isn't a `VCSRemoteAction`. `activate` is wired as the toolbar's own `.task`.

**Part 2 — live diff change kind**: `AppStore.refreshOpenDiffChangeKinds` + pure `liveChangeKind`, called from `mergeLocalStatus` and after a nav landing; `refreshingChangeKind` deleted. Writes via `TerminalSessions.refreshDiffChangeKind`, which fires no `onTabContentChange` (that records history) and returns `false` on an unchanged kind. Kept the field: `.commit` diffs need a kind live status can't supply, and `DiffViewer` has no store.

**Part 3**: TODOS corrected — struck finding (1) with the `mergeRemotes` reason, marked 5/6/7 shipped with the reasoning, moved the diff entry into **Recently done**.

**Verification**
- `make app-lint` clean; full unit suite **1968 passed / 0 failed** (11 new tests across 4 classes).
- 2 new XCUITests (`VCSToolbarGitUITests`, new `-WorkroomUITestSyncReadFailure` fixture seam) pass; scoped run only.
- Live, isolated `$HOME` + throwaway repo: `git switch -c scratch-branch` in the workroom → toolbar **and** the pane footer (a pure `branchName` reader) both followed within one sweep; `chmod 000 .git/config` → toolbar showed "Try Again / warning: unable to access…" instead of "No repository", and clicking it after restoring perms cleared back to normal.

One gap, stated plainly: the diff-tab kind refresh is verified at the store level (open-tab descriptor updates, no history entry, no-op guard) but **not** live — synthetic clicks don't reach this app's SwiftUI rows, and a UI test would need test-only fixture machinery to mutate a file's kind mid-session. Also `DiffViewer` only paints the change letter when `showsFileHeader` is on, so in a plain diff tab the user-visible effect is the "Open file in…" enablement.

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)


## Artifacts Sync (skill start)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users
# upgrading mid-stream before the migration script runs.
if [ -f "$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt" ]; then
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt"
else
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt"
fi
_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync"
_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# /sync-gbrain context-load: teach the agent to use gbrain when it's available.
# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
```

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Step 0: Detect platform and base branch

First, detect the git hosting platform from the remote URL:

```bash
git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null
```

- If the URL contains "github.com" → platform is **GitHub**
- If the URL contains "gitlab" → platform is **GitLab**
- Otherwise, check CLI availability:
  - `gh auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitHub** (covers GitHub Enterprise)
  - `glab auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitLab** (covers self-hosted)
  - Neither → **unknown** (use git-native commands only)

Determine which branch this PR/MR targets, or the repo's default branch if no
PR/MR exists. Use the result as "the base branch" in all subsequent steps.

**If GitHub:**
1. `gh pr view --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName` — if succeeds, use it
2. `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name` — if succeeds, use it

**If GitLab:**
1. `glab mr view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `target_branch` field — if succeeds, use it
2. `glab repo view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `default_branch` field — if succeeds, use it

**Git-native fallback (if unknown platform, or CLI commands fail):**
1. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|refs/remotes/origin/||'`
2. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/main 2>/dev/null` → use `main`
3. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/master 2>/dev/null` → use `master`

If all fail, fall back to `main`.

Print the detected base branch name. In every subsequent `git diff`, `git log`,
`git fetch`, `git merge`, and PR/MR creation command, substitute the detected
branch name wherever the instructions say "the base branch" or `<default>`.

# Pre-Landing PR Review

You are running the `/review` workflow. Analyze the current branch's diff against the base branch for structural issues that tests don't catch.

## Step 1: Check branch

1. Run `git branch --show-current` to get the current branch.
2. If on the base branch, output: **"Nothing to review — you're on the base branch or have no changes against it."** and stop.
3. Run `git fetch origin <base> --quiet && DIFF_BASE=$(git merge-base origin/<base> HEAD) && git diff "$DIFF_BASE" --stat` to check if there's a diff. If no diff, output the same message and stop.

---

## Step 1.5: Scope Drift Detection

Before reviewing code quality, check: **did they build what was requested — nothing more, nothing less?**

1. Read `TODOS.md` (if it exists). Read PR description (`gh pr view --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true`).
   Read commit messages (`git log origin/<base>..HEAD --oneline`).
   **If no PR exists:** rely on commit messages and TODOS.md for stated intent — this is the common case since /review runs before /ship creates the PR.
2. Identify the **stated intent** — what was this branch supposed to accomplish?
3. Run `DIFF_BASE=$(git merge-base origin/<base> HEAD) && git diff "$DIFF_BASE" --stat` and compare the files changed against the stated intent.

4. Evaluate with skepticism (incorporating plan completion results if available from an earlier step or adjacent section):

   **SCOPE CREEP detection:**
   - Files changed that are unrelated to the stated intent
   - New features or refactors not mentioned in the plan
   - "While I was in there..." changes that expand blast radius

   **MISSING REQUIREMENTS detection:**
   - Requirements from TODOS.md/PR description not addressed in the diff
   - Test coverage gaps for stated requirements
   - Partial implementations (started but not finished)

5. Output (before the main review begins):
   \`\`\`
   Scope Check: [CLEAN / DRIFT DETECTED / REQUIREMENTS MISSING]
   Intent: <1-line summary of what was requested>
   Delivered: <1-line summary of what the diff actually does>
   [If drift: list each out-of-scope change]
   [If missing: list each unaddressed requirement]
   \`\`\`

6. This is **INFORMATIONAL** — does not block the review. Proceed to the next step.
